content: CyberPeace Institute 2023 # Types of cyber incidents targeting entities in the Russian Federation July- September 2023 In alignment with the overall decline in malicious activities detected by the CyberPeace Institute in Q3 of 2023, the documented cyberattacks against entities in the Russian Federation have decreased by 72.9% compared to the previous quarter, Q2 of 2023 Additionally there has been a notable reduction of 43.8% in the number of targeted sectors and a 16.7% decrease in the number of active threat actors | Defacement | DDoS | Unknown | --------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------- | 30.8% | 53.8% | Hack and Leak | # Notable incidents in Russian Federation Disruption July 10, 2023 Confirmed cyberattack against the information system of a Russian regional medicinal distributor The cyberattack led to a disruption in sales of medicine A year of analyzing cyberattacks in comparison to the same quarter in the previous year (Q3, 2022), there has also been a decline of 72.9% of incidents A shift in the entities being targeted is evident when comparing Q3 of 2022 to Q3 of 2023 Pro-Ukrainian threat actors, during Q3 of 2022 predominantly targeted Russian media financial and administrative/support sectors However in Q3 of 2023 the focus shifted to Russian public administration transportation and ICT sectors July 23, 2023 Confirmed DDoS attack claimed by the IT Army of Ukraine against the servers of a Russian Internet service provider operating in the illegally annexed territories of Luhansk26 August 9, 2023 Confirmed DDoS attack claimed by the IT Army of Ukraine against the servers of a Russian Internet service provider operating in the illegally annexed territories of Luhansk28 September 8, 2023 Confirmed DDoS attack against the servers of a Russian IT company assisting in online voting The DDoS attack led to delays for voters in receiving SMS messages needed to vote The landscape of pro-Ukrainian threat actors targeting entities in the Russian Federation has undergone substantial changes since Q3 of 2022 During the initial analysis of malicious cyber operations within the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, the IT Army of Ukraine was notably active peaking between August and October of 2022 with 25 claimed attacks throughout that period compared to only 3 documented claims of attacks in the third quarter of 2023 TLP:

metadata.title: NATO Funds Startups Aiming to Solve Cyber Problems in Infrastructure​
metadata.keywords: NATO, startups, cybersecurity, infrastructure, defence, innovation, funding, cyber resilience, defence sectors, public-private partnerships

additional_metadata.General information about Best Practices: NATO is funding startups that focus on addressing cybersecurity issues within critical infrastructure, a key concern for both defence and civilian sectors. This initiative is part of a broader effort to enhance Europe's cyber resilience, fostering collaboration between defence forces and the private sector.
additional_metadata.Time coverage: Current initiatives with long-term goals of sustained collaboration and cyber defence improvements.
additional_metadata.Geographic coverage: Primarily Europe, with broader implications for NATO member states globally.
additional_metadata.Primary objective: To enhance cybersecurity within critical infrastructure by supporting innovative startups.
additional_metadata.Secondary objective: To strengthen the collaboration between NATO, startups, and defence organisations in developing cyber solutions.
additional_metadata.Implementation strategy: Funding startups and fostering innovation through collaborative efforts to address cyber resilience and security.
additional_metadata.Success factors: Strong NATO backing, innovative technologies, and successful integration into critical infrastructure systems.
additional_metadata.Challenges: Ensuring broad adoption and addressing the complex cybersecurity needs of both military and civilian infrastructures.
additional_metadata.Alignment with EU Policies: Aligns with European cybersecurity policies and initiatives focused on enhancing digital resilience.
additional_metadata.Transferability: The models developed can potentially be applied to other regions, particularly NATO member states, though specific challenges may arise in non-EU countries.
additional_metadata.Comment: This score confirms the ENISA Threat Landscape Report as one of the most effective and comprehensive cybersecurity governance tools in the EU’s strategic toolkit—especially relevant for policymaking, situational awareness, and institutional capacity-building.

additional_metadata.Comments: The dual-use technology framework represents a critical governance interface between civilian and defence sectors. Although it does not entail direct operational synergy, it is vital in regulating and facilitating the secure and responsible transfer of cybersecurity-related technologies across both domains. In doing so, it contributes indirectly to the broader civil-military cybersecurity ecosystem.
